rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers with DND funding or land, or BPDA inclusionary income-restricted units, may not use blanket bans based on arrests or convictions and must review applicants case by case. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions with judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old, and may not use credit scores to approve or deny applications.
rules.key_value: Convictions more than 5 years old may not be considered
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, February 2017)
rules.status_basis: Document dated February 2017; no adoption or effective date stated.

requires.name: dnd_funded_or_inclusionary
requires.text: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy

exempt_if.name: direct_relationship_or_risk
exempt_if.text: A direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought and or unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others.

exempt_if.name: current_criminal_behavior
exempt_if.text: This guidance does not apply to current criminal behavior.

exempt_if.name: conflicting_federal_state_law
exempt_if.text: Where federal or state law imposes a criminal history requirement that conflicts with a requirement of this guidance, the federal or state law preempts this policy.

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers with DND funding or land, or BPDA inclusionary income-restricted units.
coverage.exemptions_summary: The arrest and conviction limits do not apply where a conviction directly relates to the housing or poses unreasonable risk to others' safety, or to current criminal behavior. Conflicting federal or state law also preempts the policy.

precedence.text: Where federal or state law imposes a criminal history requirement that conflicts with a requirement of this guidance, the federal or state law preempts this policy.

rules.quoted_span: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis.
